A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Uncertainty-Guided (UG) framework. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite extensive reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark evaluations of UG-Search, UG-Sample and UG-Ground, alongside correlation studies, ablations and qualitative results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains original UG evaluations and adds benchmark results, efficiency measurements, filtering and prompting experiments, and larger-frame-budget analyses.

M1.justification: The entropy/BRC scoring, crop/frame selection and Kadane-based grounding procedures remain intact. V2 adds optional external prefiltering variants using YOLOv8, SAM2, DINOv2 and SigLIP, plus a visual-prompt variant that changes scoring inputs. Scorer-generator decoupling already existed in v1; newly documented KV caching does not establish when that implementation changed.

E1.justification: V2 adds GQA for compositional image reasoning and ActivityNet-QA for free-form video question answering within the existing task families. TextVQA, POPE, DocVQA, EgoSchema and NextQA are largely promoted from v1's Appendix F, not newly added coverage. MME-RealWorld and the subtitle-enabled Video-MME scenario remain.

E2.justification: V2 removes reported comparisons with GPT-4o, Gemini 1.5 Flash, SEAL, DyFo and DeepEyes from visual search, Frame-Voyager from video QA, and VTG-GPT, TFVTG, TAG and VTimeLLM-7B from grounding. These comparisons are not restored in its appendices. Rel-att becomes ViCrop with the same citation and scores, so that is a rename.

E3.justification: V2 adds throughput evaluation, Qwen2.5-VL video/grounding configurations, top-32 prefiltering, and larger-frame-budget protocols using 2 FPS and non-overlapping five-frame scoring windows. It reports half-image crops for standard QA, whereas v1 gives a general one-sixth rule; unchanged scores do not establish reruns. The main eight-of-256 frame-selection protocol remains.

E4.justification: V2 replaces the motivating zoom-in experiment with target-present versus target-absent crop analysis. It adds prefilter, visual-prompt, video-stride and maximum-frame-budget studies, and expands crop-count ablations across models. Existing scorer-decoupling and grounding-stride analyses gain throughput measurements rather than being wholly new analyses. Original qualitative failure cases remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or a specified significance-testing procedure. Appendix B retains the same Pearson correlations. V2 calls its new crop separation statistically significant but supplies no test or p-value; model-output entropy itself is not experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial benchmark, throughput, prefilter, prompting and frame-budget results while removing comparator rows and much of the visual-search subtask breakdown. Most shared scores remain unchanged. InternVL2.5's EgoSchema baseline/UG scores change from 56.3/57.1 in v1 Table 10 to 49.2/50.0 in v2 Table 4 without an explained setting change. V2's consolidated Qwen search scores use v1 Table 2's values instead of its conflicting Table 1 values.

T1.justification: V1 Appendix C offers an informal information-bottleneck interpretation and explicitly disclaims a formal guarantee. V2 replaces this with definitions, an information-bottleneck objective, entropy/mutual-information derivations, a calibration-ranking assumption, and Theorem 1 with a proof. The argument relies on approximately constant compression across candidates and preserved entropy rankings.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a unified, training-free, model-agnostic framework using intrinsic uncertainty to localize relevant evidence across visual search, long-video understanding and temporal grounding, with competitive performance against specialized methods. Reframing the first contribution around localization and adding supporting experiments do not materially change these central claims.

C2.justification: V2 develops a substantive account of inference-cost limitations and accuracy-throughput tradeoffs, distinguishes the usefulness of image versus video prefilters, and discusses maximum-context behavior. It adds model-dependent explanations for multi-crop failures and positions UG as parallelizable test-time scaling. Appendix C also shifts from an explicitly heuristic interpretation to a conditional formal justification.

D1.justification: V2 supplies a project-code URL, NVIDIA H100 hardware information, KV-cache reuse details, benchmark splits and answer-extraction procedures, visual-prompt templates, and model token/context settings for larger-frame experiments. These substantially expand reproducibility documentation beyond v1's reliance on LMMs-Eval defaults. Newly disclosed details do not establish that earlier experiments used different implementations.

R1.justification: The central positioning of uncertainty as proactive guidance rather than post-hoc detection remains. V2 adds method-specific comparisons and applicability criticisms in Appendix D, plus citations for added benchmarks, prefilters and visual prompting. It removes references to TAG, TFVTG and VTG-GPT. Rel-att/ViCrop and publication-venue updates refer to existing works.

P1.justification: V2 extensively rewrites the main narrative, reframes Section 3.1 around localization, adds a main efficiency section and an explicit limitations discussion, and reorganizes the appendices around expanded baseline and benchmark descriptions. Several former appendix experiments move into the main text. Token Entropy is renamed Average Entropy without changing its formula.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a substantially different page format and table organization. Figure 1 is replaced by distributions and heatmaps; Figure 3 gains throughput axes; Tables 1 and 4 consolidate main and appendix results. New efficiency, filtering and prompting tables and a frame-budget figure are added. Qualitative figures are reformatted and renumbered while retaining their examples.

improvement.justification: V2 improves practical assessability through measured throughput, accuracy-cost tradeoffs, larger-frame tests and substantially fuller implementation documentation. V1 largely left computational cost unquantified. These benefits are tempered by removing several specialized baselines and detailed subtask results, which weakens comparative scrutiny. The new theory remains conditional on strong calibration and constant-compression premises, so its formal presentation alone does not establish stronger validity. Overall, the gains in transparency and evaluation support a limited net improvement.
